先读取 Tokage 共享上下文和项目规则，再检查会话视图及它实际导入的滚动辅助代码；此任务明确要求只读，我不会改动或提交文件。

项目里的 `.tokage/context.md` 当前不存在；视图本身没有导入专用滚动 hook 或 helper，滚动逻辑直接写在 `SessionHistoryView`。我继续读 transcript 渲染区和相关测试/证据，核实加载、错误、工具展开和流结束时的实际行为。

### What was completed

1. `SessionHistoryView` owns the scroll behavior directly; it imports no dedicated session scroll helper.
2. The component keeps `transcriptRef` for the scroll container.
3. `followLatestRef` stores whether new content should keep the reader at the bottom.
4. `showLatest` controls whether the return button is rendered.
5. The attempt-list effect clears the current selection when the session, project, or scope changes.
6. That effect loads attempts through `pollHistory`.
7. Its success callback updates attempts and clears the loading state.
8. The success callback retains the selected attempt if it still exists in the returned list.
9. Otherwise, it selects the first returned attempt, or `null` for an empty result.
10. Its error callback ends loading and sets `attemptError`.
11. The effect cleanup stops its poller and clears `attemptReader.current`.
12. The selected-attempt effect clears `chatLogs` and `readError`.
13. It resets `followLatestRef` to `true` on each attempt change.
14. It also hides the return-to-latest button on each attempt change.
15. If no attempt is selected, it ends log loading and returns without starting a log poller.
16. Otherwise, it starts loading and calls `getChatLogs(selectedAttemptId)` through `pollHistory`.
17. Successful log reads populate `chatLogs` and clear `readError`.
18. Failed log reads end loading and set `readError`.
19. The selected-attempt effect cleanup stops its poller and clears `logReader.current`.
20. `live` reads the selected attempt’s in-memory transcript from `useTaskTranscripts`.
21. `visibleLogs` prefers `transcriptRows(live)` whenever that entry exists.
22. If there is no live entry, `visibleLogs` uses the persisted `chatLogs` snapshot.
23. This preference lets incoming in-memory updates supersede an older database snapshot.
24. The scroll observer effect runs when `selectedAttemptId` changes.
25. It exits early when the transcript container or selected attempt is missing.
26. It captures the current container in a local variable.
27. Its `active` flag starts as `true` and is set to `false` during cleanup.
28. The effect’s `update` callback first rejects inactive effects.
29. It also rejects callbacks if `transcriptRef.current` no longer points to its captured container.
30. `update` calculates distance from the bottom using scroll height, scroll top, and client height.
31. It considers the reader at the bottom when that distance is at most 32 pixels.
32. If `followLatestRef` is true, `update` scrolls to the container’s current scroll height.
33. If the reader is within 32 pixels of the bottom, `update` also resumes following.
34. In either following case, `update` hides the return button.
35. Otherwise, `update` preserves the current scroll position and shows the return button.
36. The effect creates one `ResizeObserver` for the selected attempt.
37. It observes the transcript container itself.
38. It also observes every direct child present when the effect starts.
39. A `MutationObserver` watches for child-list changes throughout the transcript subtree.
40. When nodes are removed, the mutation callback unobserves each removed element.
41. It also unobserves all descendant elements of each removed element.
42. When nodes are added, the callback observes each added element.
43. It also observes all descendant elements of each added element.
44. The mutation callback ignores records once its effect is inactive.
45. The mutation observer does not react to text-only changes within an existing node.
46. Content growth inside observed message elements can still trigger the resize observer.
47. The effect calls `update` immediately after setting up both observers.
48. Initial positioning therefore scrolls to the latest content when the default follow flag is true.
49. The scroll handler independently checks whether the reader is within 32 pixels of the bottom.
50. Scrolling near the bottom sets `followLatestRef` to `true`.
51. Scrolling above that threshold sets `followLatestRef` to `false`.
52. The scroll handler shows the return button only when above the threshold and messages exist.
53. During streaming, `visibleLogs.map` renders updates keyed by `log.messageId`.
54. A changed transcript can update message text without restarting the observer effect.
55. The rendered `data-stream-size` reflects displayed content length and serialized parts length.
56. That attribute changes with stream text or parts, while the message key can stay stable.
57. The scroll container disables browser scroll anchoring with `[overflow-anchor:none]`.
58. This leaves bottom-following and reading-position behavior to the component’s own logic.
59. `returnToLatest` exits without action if the container ref is unavailable.
60. Otherwise, it turns following on and sets `scrollTop` to `scrollHeight`.
61. It then hides the return button.
62. The button is a native `button` with an accessible translated `aria-label`.
63. It is rendered only while `showLatest` is true.
64. `loadingLogs && !live` displays a loading indicator in the transcript.
65. If live transcript data exists, that loading indicator is suppressed.
66. When there are no visible messages, the view renders a task-aware empty state.
67. The empty state distinguishes attempts with a task ID from attempts without one.
68. An empty transcript does not expose the return button because the scroll handler requires messages.
69. A log read failure displays the translated read-error alert.
70. An attempt-list failure is also surfaced through the same alert expression when an attempt is selected.
71. A live persistence error selects the persistence-error translation for the alert.
72. The alert can appear alongside the transcript; it does not reset the scroll intent.
73. `hasProcess` is true when a message has reasoning parts or tool parts.
74. Process details render inside native `<details>` and `<summary>` elements.
75. Tool details use nested native `<details>` elements, so their summaries are keyboard operable.
76. Expanding or collapsing process details changes transcript geometry within observed message elements.
77. Resize notifications caused by that geometry change run through the existing `update` callback.
78. If following is active, tool expansion or collapse can keep the transcript pinned to the bottom.
79. If the reader is above the threshold, the resize callback preserves their position and shows the return button.
80. The persisted attempt `status` is displayed in the header, but the scroll logic does not branch on it.
81. No special scroll action occurs when a stream ends; updates simply stop and the existing observers remain until selection changes or the component unmounts.
82. On attempt change, cleanup marks the previous effect inactive and disconnects both observers.
83. A queued resize callback from the old effect returns immediately after cleanup because `active` is false.
84. On unmount, the same cleanup disconnects the observers and prevents queued callbacks from acting.
85. `SessionHistoryView.test.tsx` includes a rendered-DOM test that applies 100 transcript updates and checks for one resize observer construction.
86. That test also changes the container’s mocked scroll height and fires the observer callback to check bottom following.
87. Another rendered-DOM test checks unobserving a removed message target and ignores a saved callback after switching attempts.
88. The test suite also checks initial following, reading above, return-to-latest, empty and error states, and attempt reset.
89. No imported scroll helper exists to inspect in this checkout; the only scroll implementation found is in `SessionHistoryView`.
90. The instructed `.tokage/context.md` file is absent in this checkout.

### What was completed

1. `SessionHistoryView` owns the scroll behavior directly; it imports no dedicated session scroll helper.
2. The component keeps `transcriptRef` for the scroll container.
3. `followLatestRef` stores whether new content should keep the reader at the bottom.
4. `showLatest` controls whether the return button is rendered.
5. The attempt-list effect clears the current selection when the session, project, or scope changes.
6. That effect loads attempts through `pollHistory`.
7. Its success callback updates attempts and clears the loading state.
8. The success callback retains the selected attempt if it still exists in the returned list.
9. Otherwise, it selects the first returned attempt, or `null` for an empty result.
10. Its error callback ends loading and sets `attemptError`.
11. The effect cleanup stops its poller and clears `attemptReader.current`.
12. The selected-attempt effect clears `chatLogs` and `readError`.
13. It resets `followLatestRef` to `true` on each attempt change.
14. It also hides the return-to-latest button on each attempt change.
15. If no attempt is selected, it ends log loading and returns without starting a log poller.
16. Otherwise, it starts loading and calls `getChatLogs(selectedAttemptId)` through `pollHistory`.
17. Successful log reads populate `chatLogs` and clear `readError`.
18. Failed log reads end loading and set `readError`.
19. The selected-attempt effect cleanup stops its poller and clears `logReader.current`.
20. `live` reads the selected attempt’s in-memory transcript from `useTaskTranscripts`.
21. `visibleLogs` prefers `transcriptRows(live)` whenever that entry exists.
22. If there is no live entry, `visibleLogs` uses the persisted `chatLogs` snapshot.
23. This preference lets incoming in-memory updates supersede an older database snapshot.
24. The scroll observer effect runs when `selectedAttemptId` changes.
25. It exits early when the transcript container or selected attempt is missing.
26. It captures the current container in a local variable.
27. Its `active` flag starts as `true` and is set to `false` during cleanup.
28. The effect’s `update` callback first rejects inactive effects.
29. It also rejects callbacks if `transcriptRef.current` no longer points to its captured container.
30. `update` calculates distance from the bottom using scroll height, scroll top, and client height.
31. It considers the reader at the bottom when that distance is at most 32 pixels.
32. If `followLatestRef` is true, `update` scrolls to the container’s current scroll height.
33. If the reader is within 32 pixels of the bottom, `update` also resumes following.
34. In either following case, `update` hides the return button.
35. Otherwise, `update` preserves the current scroll position and shows the return button.
36. The effect creates one `ResizeObserver` for the selected attempt.
37. It observes the transcript container itself.
38. It also observes every direct child present when the effect starts.
39. A `MutationObserver` watches for child-list changes throughout the transcript subtree.
40. When nodes are removed, the mutation callback unobserves each removed element.
41. It also unobserves all descendant elements of each removed element.
42. When nodes are added, the callback observes each added element.
43. It also observes all descendant elements of each added element.
44. The mutation callback ignores records once its effect is inactive.
45. The mutation observer does not react to text-only changes within an existing node.
46. Content growth inside observed message elements can still trigger the resize observer.
47. The effect calls `update` immediately after setting up both observers.
48. Initial positioning therefore scrolls to the latest content when the default follow flag is true.
49. The scroll handler independently checks whether the reader is within 32 pixels of the bottom.
50. Scrolling near the bottom sets `followLatestRef` to `true`.
51. Scrolling above that threshold sets `followLatestRef` to `false`.
52. The scroll handler shows the return button only when above the threshold and messages exist.
53. During streaming, `visibleLogs.map` renders updates keyed by `log.messageId`.
54. A changed transcript can update message text without restarting the observer effect.
55. The rendered `data-stream-size` reflects displayed content length and serialized parts length.
56. That attribute changes with stream text or parts, while the message key can stay stable.
57. The scroll container disables browser scroll anchoring with `[overflow-anchor:none]`.
58. This leaves bottom-following and reading-position behavior to the component’s own logic.
59. `returnToLatest` exits without action if the container ref is unavailable.
60. Otherwise, it turns following on and sets `scrollTop` to `scrollHeight`.
61. It then hides the return button.
62. The button is a native `button` with an accessible translated `aria-label`.
63. It is rendered only while `showLatest` is true.
64. `loadingLogs && !live` displays a loading indicator in the transcript.
65. If live transcript data exists, that loading indicator is suppressed.
66. When there are no visible messages, the view renders a task-aware empty state.
67. The empty state distinguishes attempts with a task ID from attempts without one.
68. An empty transcript does not expose the return button because the scroll handler requires messages.
69. A log read failure displays the translated read-error alert.
70. An attempt-list failure is also surfaced through the same alert expression when an attempt is selected.
71. A live persistence error selects the persistence-error translation for the alert.
72. The alert can appear alongside the transcript; it does not reset the scroll intent.
73. `hasProcess` is true when a message has reasoning parts or tool parts.
74. Process details render inside native `<details>` and `<summary>` elements.
75. Tool details use nested native `<details>` elements, so their summaries are keyboard operable.
76. Expanding or collapsing process details changes transcript geometry within observed message elements.
77. Resize notifications caused by that geometry change run through the existing `update` callback.
78. If following is active, tool expansion or collapse can keep the transcript pinned to the bottom.
79. If the reader is above the threshold, the resize callback preserves their position and shows the return button.
80. The persisted attempt `status` is displayed in the header, but the scroll logic does not branch on it.
81. No special scroll action occurs when a stream ends; updates simply stop and the existing observers remain until selection changes or the component unmounts.
82. On attempt change, cleanup marks the previous effect inactive and disconnects both observers.
83. A queued resize callback from the old effect returns immediately after cleanup because `active` is false.
84. On unmount, the same cleanup disconnects the observers and prevents queued callbacks from acting.
85. `SessionHistoryView.test.tsx` includes a rendered-DOM test that applies 100 transcript updates and checks for one resize observer construction.
86. That test also changes the container’s mocked scroll height and fires the observer callback to check bottom following.
87. Another rendered-DOM test checks unobserving a removed message target and ignores a saved callback after switching attempts.
88. The test suite also checks initial following, reading above, return-to-latest, empty and error states, and attempt reset.
89. No imported scroll helper exists to inspect in this checkout; the only scroll implementation found is in `SessionHistoryView`.
90. The instructed `.tokage/context.md` file is absent in this checkout.

先读取 Tokage 共享上下文和项目规则，再检查会话视图及它实际导入的滚动辅助代码；此任务明确要求只读，我不会改动或提交文件。

项目里的 `.tokage/context.md` 当前不存在；视图本身没有导入专用滚动 hook 或 helper，滚动逻辑直接写在 `SessionHistoryView`。我继续读 transcript 渲染区和相关测试/证据，核实加载、错误、工具展开和流结束时的实际行为。

### What was completed

1. `SessionHistoryView` owns the scroll behavior directly; it imports no dedicated session scroll helper.
2. The component keeps `transcriptRef` for the scroll container.
3. `followLatestRef` stores whether new content should keep the reader at the bottom.
4. `showLatest` controls whether the return button is rendered.
5. The attempt-list effect clears the current selection when the session, project, or scope changes.
6. That effect loads attempts through `pollHistory`.
7. Its success callback updates attempts and clears the loading state.
8. The success callback retains the selected attempt if it still exists in the returned list.
9. Otherwise, it selects the first returned attempt, or `null` for an empty result.
10. Its error callback ends loading and sets `attemptError`.
11. The effect cleanup stops its poller and clears `attemptReader.current`.
12. The selected-attempt effect clears `chatLogs` and `readError`.
13. It resets `followLatestRef` to `true` on each attempt change.
14. It also hides the return-to-latest button on each attempt change.
15. If no attempt is selected, it ends log loading and returns without starting a log poller.
16. Otherwise, it starts loading and calls `getChatLogs(selectedAttemptId)` through `pollHistory`.
17. Successful log reads populate `chatLogs` and clear `readError`.
18. Failed log reads end loading and set `readError`.
19. The selected-attempt effect cleanup stops its poller and clears `logReader.current`.
20. `live` reads the selected attempt’s in-memory transcript from `useTaskTranscripts`.
21. `visibleLogs` prefers `transcriptRows(live)` whenever that entry exists.
22. If there is no live entry, `visibleLogs` uses the persisted `chatLogs` snapshot.
23. This preference lets incoming in-memory updates supersede an older database snapshot.
24. The scroll observer effect runs when `selectedAttemptId` changes.
25. It exits early when the transcript container or selected attempt is missing.
26. It captures the current container in a local variable.
27. Its `active` flag starts as `true` and is set to `false` during cleanup.
28. The effect’s `update` callback first rejects inactive effects.
29. It also rejects callbacks if `transcriptRef.current` no longer points to its captured container.
30. `update` calculates distance from the bottom using scroll height, scroll top, and client height.
31. It considers the reader at the bottom when that distance is at most 32 pixels.
32. If `followLatestRef` is true, `update` scrolls to the container’s current scroll height.
33. If the reader is within 32 pixels of the bottom, `update` also resumes following.
34. In either following case, `update` hides the return button.
35. Otherwise, `update` preserves the current scroll position and shows the return button.
36. The effect creates one `ResizeObserver` for the selected attempt.
37. It observes the transcript container itself.
38. It also observes every direct child present when the effect starts.
39. A `MutationObserver` watches for child-list changes throughout the transcript subtree.
40. When nodes are removed, the mutation callback unobserves each removed element.
41. It also unobserves all descendant elements of each removed element.
42. When nodes are added, the callback observes each added element.
43. It also observes all descendant elements of each added element.
44. The mutation callback ignores records once its effect is inactive.
45. The mutation observer does not react to text-only changes within an existing node.
46. Content growth inside observed message elements can still trigger the resize observer.
47. The effect calls `update` immediately after setting up both observers.
48. Initial positioning therefore scrolls to the latest content when the default follow flag is true.
49. The scroll handler independently checks whether the reader is within 32 pixels of the bottom.
50. Scrolling near the bottom sets `followLatestRef` to `true`.
51. Scrolling above that threshold sets `followLatestRef` to `false`.
52. The scroll handler shows the return button only when above the threshold and messages exist.
53. During streaming, `visibleLogs.map` renders updates keyed by `log.messageId`.
54. A changed transcript can update message text without restarting the observer effect.
55. The rendered `data-stream-size` reflects displayed content length and serialized parts length.
56. That attribute changes with stream text or parts, while the message key can stay stable.
57. The scroll container disables browser scroll anchoring with `[overflow-anchor:none]`.
58. This leaves bottom-following and reading-position behavior to the component’s own logic.
59. `returnToLatest` exits without action if the container ref is unavailable.
60. Otherwise, it turns following on and sets `scrollTop` to `scrollHeight`.
61. It then hides the return button.
62. The button is a native `button` with an accessible translated `aria-label`.
63. It is rendered only while `showLatest` is true.
64. `loadingLogs && !live` displays a loading indicator in the transcript.
65. If live transcript data exists, that loading indicator is suppressed.
66. When there are no visible messages, the view renders a task-aware empty state.
67. The empty state distinguishes attempts with a task ID from attempts without one.
68. An empty transcript does not expose the return button because the scroll handler requires messages.
69. A log read failure displays the translated read-error alert.
70. An attempt-list failure is also surfaced through the same alert expression when an attempt is selected.
71. A live persistence error selects the persistence-error translation for the alert.
72. The alert can appear alongside the transcript; it does not reset the scroll intent.
73. `hasProcess` is true when a message has reasoning parts or tool parts.
74. Process details render inside native `<details>` and `<summary>` elements.
75. Tool details use nested native `<details>` elements, so their summaries are keyboard operable.
76. Expanding or collapsing process details changes transcript geometry within observed message elements.
77. Resize notifications caused by that geometry change run through the existing `update` callback.
78. If following is active, tool expansion or collapse can keep the transcript pinned to the bottom.
79. If the reader is above the threshold, the resize callback preserves their position and shows the return button.
80. The persisted attempt `status` is displayed in the header, but the scroll logic does not branch on it.
81. No special scroll action occurs when a stream ends; updates simply stop and the existing observers remain until selection changes or the component unmounts.
82. On attempt change, cleanup marks the previous effect inactive and disconnects both observers.
83. A queued resize callback from the old effect returns immediately after cleanup because `active` is false.
84. On unmount, the same cleanup disconnects the observers and prevents queued callbacks from acting.
85. `SessionHistoryView.test.tsx` includes a rendered-DOM test that applies 100 transcript updates and checks for one resize observer construction.
86. That test also changes the container’s mocked scroll height and fires the observer callback to check bottom following.
87. Another rendered-DOM test checks unobserving a removed message target and ignores a saved callback after switching attempts.
88. The test suite also checks initial following, reading above, return-to-latest, empty and error states, and attempt reset.
89. No imported scroll helper exists to inspect in this checkout; the only scroll implementation found is in `SessionHistoryView`.
90. The instructed `.tokage/context.md` file is absent in this checkout.
